accepted.label: Monte Carlo Simulation Definition and Process
accepted.description: Monte Carlo simulation is a stochastic method that assigns probability distributions to uncertain inputs, uses random sampling to generate thousands of simulated outcomes, and analyzes the full distribution of possible results to support decision-making under uncertainty. It involves defining input distributions, running iterations, aggregating results, and interpreting output distributions (e.g., via frequency histograms).
coverage_criteria: Define Monte Carlo simulation and explain how it differs from deterministic modeling.
List the steps of Monte Carlo simulation and describe how to interpret the output distribution.
accepted.merge_rationale: Both candidates describe the same core concept: Monte Carlo simulation as a process using probability distributions and random sampling to generate outcome distributions. The minor differences (e.g., wording, emphasis on risk assessment vs. decision-making tools) do not constitute a different teachable idea at the same level of understanding. They present the same definition and steps, so they are merged into one subject concept.
